name: NJ-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 13 points on the PVI
Democratic candidate holds an overwhelming money advantage (about $3.5 million raised plus outside support vs. $79,000 for the Republican)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 96 percent
Open seat with no public polls or expert ratings to confirm the picture
model.rationale: An open seat in a D+13 district with a Democrat outraising the Republican by more than 19-to-1 and market pricing near 96 percent leaves little realistic path for a GOP upset, so the fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
model.watch: Any public polling showing the district swinging sharply toward Republicans, or a late surge of outside spending behind Mele, would be the first signal of a tighter race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Bonnie Watson Coleman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
New Jersey's 12th District sits in the state's solidly Democratic central corridor, with a partisan lean of about 13 points toward Democrats. Longtime incumbent Bonnie Watson Coleman is retiring, leaving an open seat, but the district's underlying fundamentals continue to favor the Democratic side by a wide margin.

Democrat Adam Hamawy has raised over $1.5 million and draws roughly $1.9 million in outside support, while Republican Gregg Mele has raised under $80,000 with only a few thousand dollars on hand. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96 percent. With no public polling or expert ratings available, the assessment rests on the district's lean, the stark resource gap, and market pricing, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold.
